scenes.tts: Can the gate from chapter one fail while every gatekeeper remains present? The purple inhibitory neuron, its ending, and the red target all remain. This time, the change occurs inside the target neuron.
scenes.visual: Rebuild chapter one's mouse dorsal-horn circuit at the same positions and colours. Cell-count ticks confirm the purple neuron remains. Zoom into its ending on the red target while blue and orange pulses continue moving in the background. Label the picture 'mechanism schematic'.
scenes.narration: Can the gate from chapter one fail while every gatekeeper remains present? The purple inhibitory neuron, its ending, and the red target all remain. This time, the change occurs inside the target neuron.

scenes.visual: Keep the intact purple-to-red synapse moving. The title 'When Inhibition Changes Sign' grows from the synaptic gap, then clears as the camera moves through the red membrane.

scenes.tts: An inhibitory synapse opens channels permeable to chloride and bicarbonate. Its current depends on the difference between membrane potential and anion reversal potential. Teal K C C two helps keep intracellular chloride low in these spinal neurons.
scenes.caption: An inhibitory synapse opens channels permeable to chloride and bicarbonate. Its current depends on the difference between membrane potential and anion reversal potential. Teal KCC2 helps keep intracellular chloride low in these spinal neurons.
scenes.visual: Show a large red target membrane, one purple terminal and a labelled anion channel as simple blocks. Teal KCC2 blocks move chloride dots outward. A voltage ruler places anion reversal below membrane potential. No molecular structures.
scenes.narration: An inhibitory synapse opens channels permeable to chloride and bicarbonate. Its current depends on the difference between membrane potential and anion reversal potential. Teal KCC2 helps keep intracellular chloride low in these spinal neurons.

scenes.tts: In adult male rats, nerve injury reduced dorsal-horn K C C two. In acute lamina one slices, anion reversal shifted in the depolarizing direction. The same synaptic conductance now produced current with a different sign.
scenes.caption: In adult male rats, nerve injury reduced dorsal-horn KCC2. In acute lamina I slices, anion reversal shifted in the depolarizing direction. The same synaptic conductance now produced current with a different sign.
scenes.visual: Fade some teal KCC2 blocks without removing the purple ending. Chloride dots accumulate inside. On the voltage ruler, slide the reversal marker upward across membrane potential. Transform the driving-force arrow from +10 to −15 millivolts, computed on screen in the next scene.
scenes.narration: In adult male rats, nerve injury reduced dorsal-horn KCC2. In acute lamina I slices, anion reversal shifted in the depolarizing direction. The same synaptic conductance now produced current with a different sign.

scenes.tts: Use one computed case at a membrane potential of minus sixty-five millivolts. Reversal at minus seventy-five gives plus ten millivolts of driving force. Move reversal to minus fifty, and driving force becomes minus fifteen. Conductance stayed fixed. Current direction changed.
scenes.caption: Use one computed case at a membrane potential of −65 mV. Reversal at −75 mV gives +10 mV of driving force. Move reversal to −50 mV, and driving force becomes −15 mV. Conductance stayed fixed. Current direction changed.
scenes.visual: Make the voltage ruler fill most of the frame. Compute Vm minus Eanion on screen with labelled blocks, first −65 − (−75) = +10, then −65 − (−50) = −15. Transform one current arrow through zero as the reversal marker moves.
scenes.narration: Use one computed case at a membrane potential of −65 mV. Reversal at −75 mV gives +10 mV of driving force. Move reversal to −50 mV, and driving force becomes −15 mV. Conductance stayed fixed. Current direction changed.

scenes.tts: Current reversal is not the whole claim. An open anion conductance can still shunt other current. A depolarizing response becomes excitatory only if its net effect raises firing. The rat experiments measured increased excitability too.
scenes.visual: Keep the same membrane. One incoming orange current is partly shunted through the open purple channel. Then move the reversal marker farther and animate the red firing gauge rising. Label both panels 'schematic'; keep the current values only on the computed ruler.
scenes.narration: Current reversal is not the whole claim. An open anion conductance can still shunt other current. A depolarizing response becomes excitatory only if its net effect raises firing. The rat experiments measured increased excitability too.

scenes.tts: Now predict the diagnostic pattern. Cell counts remain stable after injury. Which added measurement can reveal a changed postsynaptic effect: more counting, an evoked output recording, or anion reversal measured without replacing chloride?
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the intact circuit. Place three large instrument icons beneath stable cell counts: another counter, an evoked-current trace, and a gramicidin perforated-patch electrode beside a voltage ruler. Keep all unselected.
scenes.narration: Now predict the diagnostic pattern. Cell counts remain stable after injury. Which added measurement can reveal a changed postsynaptic effect: more counting, an evoked output recording, or anion reversal measured without replacing chloride?

scenes.visual: Hold the question and three instruments. Animate only slow chloride drift and a four-and-a-half-second thinking timer. Do not reveal the answer.

scenes.tts: Measure anion reversal with a gramicidin perforated patch. It gives electrical access while preserving the cell's chloride. Stable counts test survival. Evoked inhibitory events test output. Reversal tests the target's response to that output.
scenes.visual: Highlight the perforated-patch icon. Show its pore admitting electrical access while chloride dots remain inside. Build a three-row table by transforming the icons: cells to 'survival', evoked events to 'output', reversal ruler to 'postsynaptic effect'.
scenes.narration: Measure anion reversal with a gramicidin perforated patch. It gives electrical access while preserving the cell's chloride. Stable counts test survival. Evoked inhibitory events test output. Reversal tests the target's response to that output.

scenes.tts: The rat studies also traced the signal upstream. A T P stimulated microglia released B D N F. Gold B D N F blocks then reached Trk B on the red target.
scenes.caption: The rat studies also traced the signal upstream. ATP-stimulated microglia released BDNF. Gold BDNF blocks then reached TrkB on the red target.
scenes.visual: Carry the red target and add a gold cartoon microglial cell. Gold BDNF blocks leave it and travel to a labelled TrkB block on the target. Keep the reversal marker visible but stationary.
scenes.narration: The rat studies also traced the signal upstream. ATP-stimulated microglia released BDNF. Gold BDNF blocks then reached TrkB on the red target.

scenes.tts: Gold B D N F then moved the reversal marker in the target. These rat transfer experiments did not measure K C C two afterwards. The purple synapse remained present throughout the shift.
scenes.caption: Gold BDNF then moved the reversal marker in the target. These rat transfer experiments did not measure KCC2 afterwards. The purple synapse remained present throughout the shift.
scenes.visual: Carry the BDNF-to-TrkB action forward. Slide the reversal marker upward while the teal KCC2 blocks stay unchanged under a small label 'not measured here'. Keep the purple terminal, anion channel and red target continuously visible. Label the mechanism 'adult male rat studies'.
scenes.narration: Gold BDNF then moved the reversal marker in the target. These rat transfer experiments did not measure KCC2 afterwards. The purple synapse remained present throughout the shift.

scenes.tts: Compare three pure patterns. Cell death lowers the count and evoked events. Lost output leaves counts stable but reduces events. A changed postsynaptic effect leaves counts stable and events present while reversal moves. Real mechanisms can coexist.
scenes.visual: Transform the carried circuit into three large table columns. Animate only the changed row in each: death lowers cells and events; lost output lowers events; postsynaptic change moves the reversal ruler. Finish by overlapping the columns under 'can coexist'.
scenes.narration: Compare three pure patterns. Cell death lowers the count and evoked events. Lost output leaves counts stable but reduces events. A changed postsynaptic effect leaves counts stable and events present while reversal moves. Real mechanisms can coexist.

scenes.tts: This route was established in adult male rats. It is not automatically obligatory across species or sexes. Keep the experimental rule instead. Count cells, test output, then measure reversal in the target neuron.
scenes.visual: Shrink the mechanism into a bordered card labelled 'adult male rat lamina I'. Return to the three diagnostic rows. Each row lights in order while the intact purple gatekeeper remains visible and the red target's reversal ruler moves.
scenes.narration: This route was established in adult male rats. It is not automatically obligatory across species or sexes. Keep the experimental rule instead. Count cells, test output, then measure reversal in the target neuron.

scenes.visual: End card over the moving diagnostic table: 'Separate survival, output, and postsynaptic effect.' Keep the six-word rule large and centered.
